subject: ArkLight-7b elevated server errors — short status + recovery plan
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearline.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: support@clearline.ai
Date: 2027-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden 5xx surge from arklight-7b on production — need urgent help

Hi Ben / Karthik,

We're seeing a sharp rise in 5xx responses when our platform calls arklight-7b via the Redwood hosted API starting ~08:50 PDT. Error rates jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% and several customer-facing jobs are failing. Example response: "InternalServerError: kernel_execution_failure (CUDA out-of-memory?)" — see attached arklight-error-sample.log.txt.

Impact: approx 30% of inference requests during high concurrency windows are returning immediate 5xx and not retryable. This is affecting two flows that require sub-500ms latency.

Can you confirm whether this is an isolated routing/tenant issue or something model-level? We're pausing retries to avoid backpressure but need ETA on fix.

Thanks,
Marta

Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability
Clearline Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearline.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx surge from arklight-7b on production — need urgent help

Hi Marta — thanks for flagging and for the log. We're opening an urgent ticket (JIRA-SUP-1427) and looping in engineering. Short answers: we see a spike in 5xxs from the arklight-7b variant in us-west-2 starting 08:45 PDT. We're treating this as a high-priority incident and will provide a recovery ETA within 30–45 minutes.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Karh tik will validate whether traffic routing changed for your tenant.
- Marissa and Olga will triage runtime metrics and kernel selection logs.
- We'll provide a temporary recommended mitigation (fallback to arklight-7b-quant-lite or pin to a different model) if safe for your workload.

I've attached the sample log you sent and a link to the incident folder. We'll keep this thread updated.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts internal SLAs.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearline.ai>
Date: 2027-10-11T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx surge from arklight-7b on production — need urgent help

Hi all — quick triage update (ops):

What we observed:
- Elevated 5xxs across arklight-7b replicas in us-west-2 starting ~08:44 PDT.
- Error signature consistent with kernel selection failing under a micro-burst: "kernel_launch_failure -> RNN_ATTENTION_KERNEL" followed by allocator retries and eventual 5xx.
- Concurrency spike correlated with batch size growth from an upstream aggregator in one availability zone.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:10 PDT):
- Scaled out arklight-7b replica pool by +25% to reduce queuing and dropped the aggressive kernel-selection flag for the 7b runtime to force a safer execution path.
- Applied temporary routing rule to send Clearline traffic to variants: (1) arklight-7b-stable or (2) arklight-7b-quant-lite where latency profile acceptable.

Current status (09:46 PDT): error rate down from ~6% to ~0.8% for Clearline test requests. We're still monitoring for recurrence.

Next actions:
- Collect and attach scheduling/metrics CSV (attached).
- Run post-incident data collection and prepare a short RCA and recommended permanent fixes (kernel selector logic change + more conservative default batch thresholds).

M
Marissa Cole
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearline.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-11T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx surge from arklight-7b on production — need urgent help

Marta — thanks for your patience. Following Marissa's changes we saw a sustained reduction in 5xxs and validated end-to-end for the two customer workflows you called out. A few operational notes and commitments: 

- We've kept the conservative kernel-selection flag in place for the arklight-7b pool and retained the +25% replica buffer while we complete the RCA.
- We're scheduling a canary of an updated kernel selector that avoids choosing the failing execution path when memory headroom drops below 20% (target: 2027-10-15 deploy to canary).
- We'll provide a formal postmortem draft within 72 hours, include mitigations, and propose a one-off service credit for the impacted window.

If you'd like us to pin your account to arklight-7b-stable for the next 48 hours while we finish the changes, we can do that. Please confirm.

—Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearline.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-12T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: arklight-7b transient kernel-selection failure — RCA + actions

Hi Marta / Alex / Ben — final update and RCA summary: 

Summary (what happened):
- Root cause: a regression in the kernel-selection heuristic for arklight-7b introduced in 2027-09-30 runtime patch RT-1.14. The selector favored a newer attention kernel that performs faster but uses higher temporary memory. Under a micro-burst of large-batch requests from a Clearline ingestion job, GPUs hit transient memory pressure causing the kernel to fail and the runtime to return 5xx.

Impact window: 2027-10-11 08:44–09:12 PDT. Peak error rate ~6% for affected replicas.

Actions taken (completed):
- Reverted the heuristic for the arklight-7b pool (safer kernel path) and added a temporary +25% replica buffer.
- Implemented an upstream throttling recommendation for batch growth detection to prevent sudden queue growth.
- Added an automatic fallback policy: if the kernel selector observes >1% immediate failures for a kernel path, requests will fallback to a stable variant for 10 minutes.

Planned actions (by priority):
- Code: harden kernel selector with explicit memory headroom checks and backpressure signals (target: canary 2027-10-15).
- Ops: add proactive alerting rule for sudden batch-size distribution shifts (ETA: 2027-10-14).
- Customer ops: offer option to pin Clearline to arklight-7b-stable for 48 hours or stay on dynamic routing (we left the pin in place per Ben's note; confirm if you'd prefer to keep it).

Compensation: Redwood will propose a small service credit for Clearline covering the impacted time window; Ben will follow-up on terms.

Attachments: arklight-error-sample.log.txt, scheduling-metrics-20271011.csv, arklight-postmortem-draft.docx (shared).

Please let us know if you want a short sync call to walk through the RCA — happy to schedule.

Thanks for working quickly with us on this.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
